classification.difficultyReason: Identify the ladder as the hypotenuse and use cosine and sine with the angle measured from the vertical.

content.prompt: A $3\text{ m}$ ladder leans against a wall so that it makes an angle of $40^\circ$ with the vertical. Calculate answers to one decimal place.

children.label: a
children.prompt: How far up the wall does it reach?

answer.worked:
Let $h$ be the height reached up the wall. The height is adjacent to the $40^\circ$ angle and the ladder is the hypotenuse.

$$\begin{align*}\cos40^\circ&=\frac{h}{3}\\h&=3\cos40^\circ\\h&\approx2.3\text{ m}\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: How far is the foot of the ladder from the wall?

answer.worked:
Let $d$ be the distance of the foot from the wall. This distance is opposite the $40^\circ$ angle.

$$\begin{align*}\sin40^\circ&=\frac{d}{3}\\d&=3\sin40^\circ\\d&\approx1.9\text{ m}\end{align*}$$
